title: MotionGrounder: Grounded Multi-Object Motion Transfer via Diffusion Transformer
claim: A frozen generator is steered by two complementary loss modules, one for motion and one for grounding, so multiple objects follow the reference.
layout: Bottom-row main flow left-to-right; top loss modules fed by a central attention grid
description: A wide schematic with a main generation pipeline along the bottom. A noisy video latent Z_t and a caption ("A fox and a raccoon are perched on a fallen tree trunk.") enter a frozen Diffusion Transformer, drawn as green rounded bars with a snowflake icon. Its output Z_{t-1} passes through a decoder D to give the final video V_T. Above the transformer, an extracted attention map A^t is drawn as a 2x2 grid of text and video query/key blocks: text-to-text, text-to-video, video-to-text and video-to-video. Dashed arrows in matching colors route two of the blocks to the other panels. The top-left panel, the object-caption alignment loss (OCAL), shows per-object masks for "fox" and "raccoon" feeding L_OCAL. The top-right panel, the flow-based motion signal (FMS), shows a source video passing through optical flow estimation and then DISP, L_FMS and FMS(z_ref). Green headings and dashed arrows guide the eye.
caption: Overview of MotionGrounder. MotionGrounder transfers motion from the three reference videos in (a) to the synthesized videos in (b) and (c) with explicit object grounding, supporting structural and appearance changes in a training-free manner. Frames in the reference videos include color-coded bounding boxes corresponding to objects in the target captions.
abstract: Motion transfer enables controllable video generation by transferring temporal dynamics from a reference video to synthesize a new video conditioned on a target caption. However, existing Diffusion Transformer (DiT)-based methods either transfer the motion of a single object or handle multiple objects without binding each object caption to its object, restricting fine-grained control in real-world scenes. In this work, we introduce MotionGrounder, a training-free DiT-based framework that is the first to jointly handle motion transfer and object grounding in multi-object scenes. Our Flow-based Motion Signal (FMS) in MotionGrounder provides a stable motion prior for target video generation, while our Object-Caption Alignment Loss (OCAL) grounds object captions to their corresponding spatial regions. We further propose two new metrics: the Object Grounding Score (OGS), which jointly evaluates (i) spatial alignment between source video objects and their generated counterparts and (ii) semantic consistency between each generated object and its target caption, and the Motion Grounding Score (MGS), which evaluates whether each object moves like its source object at the correct location. Our experiments show that MotionGrounder improves object grounding over recent baselines, with the advantage appearing once several objects are present, across quantitative, qualitative, and human evaluations.
